title: When the Oath Turns Again
premise: Felix Amberdale has spent nine years making herself forgettable: a royal food-taster whose poison immunity is the court's best-kept secret and whose knowledge of Thornfell's smuggler roads is her only leverage. When prayers to the old gods start being answered—crops blooming overnight, dead rivers running sweet—the crown blames smugglers, but Felix recognizes the signs of something older: the court beneath the mountain is waking, and it collects souls as toll. Her little brother Tammy, sold years ago to pay their mother's debts, is among the taken, and his borrowed time is nearly spent. To steal him back, Felix must ally with a disgraced priestess, a god who answers in riddles, and the one courtier who knows her secret—all while discovering that her own immunity was never accidental: she was marked at birth as the gods' tithe, and the mountain intends to collect her too. In the end Felix trades her stolen invisibility for a new name spoken aloud before the old gods, buying Tammy's freedom with her own remembered self—and choosing found family over the safety of being no one.
about_author: Petra Montrose is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade feeding royalty-adjacent politicians and developed strong opinions about what goes into soup. She writes fantasy about people whose jobs are smaller than their courage.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She survives a poisoned plum meant for the queen, hides her immunity from the court physician, and slips out through Thornfell's smuggler roads to deliver a warning to an old fence. Establishes her invisibility as armor. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Sweetwater
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A river that ran dry for thirty years floods with drinkable water overnight; villagers leave offerings on its banks. Felix tastes the water and finds it faintly bitter—wrong. First hint the old gods are answering, but not kindly. Beat: unease beneath wonder.

chapters.title: What Mother Sold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, flashback braided with present. She visits her mother's grave and recalls the night Tammy was taken by the mountain's collectors—a debt paid in flesh. She counts the years: his soul-contract expires at midwinter. Beat: guilt sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Priestess of Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She tracks rumors to Sera Vane, a disgraced priestess of the old gods living half-mad in a shrine cave, who confirms the court beneath the mountain is stirring. Sera refuses to help—until Felix mentions Tammy's contract. Beat: reluctant alliance forged.

chapters.title: A God Answers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The two perform a divination; instead of silence, something answers—a god calling itself the Warden, speaking only in questions about names and memory. It warns: 'What was given cannot be stolen, only traded.' Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Court Intrigue, Bitter Leaf
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Back at the palace, Lord Aldric Corvane—chancellor and secret poisoner—tests her with a dish laced with something even she can't identify. He suspects what she is. She plays dumb, barely. Beat: the hunter realizes she is prey.

chapters.title: Roads Under Thornfell
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She guides Sera through smuggler tunnels toward the mountain's gate, revealing her encyclopedic knowledge of hidden ways—and why she learned them: escape routes planned for a brother who never came home. Beat: vulnerability shared.

chapters.title: The Tithe Marked Twice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera discovers an old ritual scar on Felix's shoulder matching the tithe-mark of the mountain court: Felix was promised before birth. Her immunity isn't trained—it's the mountain keeping its property healthy. Beat: identity shattered.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Corvane corners her privately: he knows about the mark, and he wants the mountain court's power for himself. He offers to help free Tammy if Felix opens the gate for him. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using a collector's token stolen from a shrine, Felix descends alone into the mountain and sees the court: beautiful, hollow-eyed souls serving a throne of roots and bone. She finds Tammy—he doesn't remember her. Beat: heartbreak at the threshold.

chapters.title: My Brother's Face
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She spends a stolen hour with memory-wiped Tammy, telling him stories of home that feel like someone else's dreams to him. A courtier-soul secretly slips her a hint: contracts can be rewritten if a greater name is offered. Beat: love persisting against erasure.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera deciphers the Warden's riddles: the mountain trades in selves, and the only currency it honors is a true name freely surrendered. Surrendering hers would unmake Sera entirely. She begins writing letters she'll never send. Beat: sacrifice contemplated.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Corvane forces the issue: he's followed her, seizes the token, and opens the gate with an army of hired blades behind him. The mountain wakes angry. Felix must choose between stopping him and reaching Tammy. Beat: everything burning at once.

chapters.title: Roots and Bone
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inside the collapsing court, Corvane offers his bargain to the throne—and the mountain accepts his name, consuming him from within as payment for his ambition. Power corrupts; the mountain simply eats it. Beat: horror as cautionary spectacle.

chapters.title: The Warden's Question
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Warden finally appears—not a monster but a tired keeper—and asks Felix directly: 'Who are you, if no one remembers you?' She realizes her invisibility was always a kind of death. Beat: the thematic question made flesh.

chapters.title: Tammy Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the chaos, Felix sings the lullaby their mother used; a fragment surfaces in Tammy, and he says her name. The contract cracks—but the mountain demands replacement: a name of equal weight. Beat: hope with a knife under it.

chapters.title: Sera's Letters
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera arrives wounded but resolute, ready to surrender her name—until Felix stops her. Found family means no one pays alone. Together they devise a third path: not one name, but many witnesses. Beat: solidarity against despair.

chapters.title: The Gathering of Witnesses
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Felix sends word down every smuggler road: everyone Tammy ever fed, sheltered, or laughed with comes to the mountain's mouth to speak his name aloud. Memory as collective act. Beat: the theme of found family made literal.

chapters.title: Midwinter Bargain
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the deadline, Felix stands before the throne and offers the trade the Warden hinted at: her own name—'Felix Amberdale'—freely given, in exchange for Tammy's contract voided. The mountain weighs it. Beat: climax of sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The trade completes strangely: the mountain takes her name but the gathered witnesses refuse to let it hold her—they speak her back into existence, each voice a thread. Tammy walks out whole; Felix walks out changed, half-remembered, half-new. Beat: triumph earned through community.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Recovery: Tammy relearning the world, Sera rebuilding her shrine with congregants, Felix tasting food again—but now for family, not kings. The Warden leaves one final question unanswered, a door left open. Beat: quiet after the storm.

chapters.title: When the Oath Turns Again
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. One year later, offerings appear on the sweetwater banks again—this time given freely, and answered gently. Felix writes her own name in the ledger of the rebuilt shrine, first entry. Being known is no longer a risk; it's the point. Beat: resolution and warmth.
